title: The Silence Before the Truth
content:
As soon as Rohini heard my voice, she fell silent. For a few long seconds, there was nothing but silence between us. Then, in a voice filled with surprise and disbelief, she finally spoke.

"Siddu...?"

"Yes," I replied softly. "It's me."

We exchanged a few words before I gathered the courage to ask the question that had been haunting me for months.

"How's Shreya?"

There was another brief silence.

Then Rohini asked quietly,

"Are you... still in love with Shreya?"

Without a moment's hesitation, I answered,

"Yes... I am."

The silence returned once again.

Something about the way she had asked that question made my heart uneasy.

"What happened?" I asked. "Why did you ask me like that?"

Rohini took a slow breath before replying.

"Because she is..."

Just as Siddu was about to reveal what Rohini had said next, his eyes drifted toward the roadside. A few meters ahead, an elderly couple stood beside their car, which appeared to have broken down. They were looking at every passing vehicle with hopeful eyes, raising their hands in the hope that someone would stop and help them.

Without giving it a second thought, Siddu leaned forward.

"Could you please stop the car?" he requested the driver.

The driver immediately pulled over.

Siddu stepped out of the cab and walked toward the elderly couple with a warm smile.

"If you don't mind, you can travel with us," he said politely.

The couple looked at each other before their worried expressions slowly transformed into grateful smiles.

"Thank you so much, son," the old man said with folded hands.

"It's alright," Siddu replied gently. "Please come in."

They happily got into the car, their faces filled with relief.

Watching everything from her seat, Sneha couldn't help but admire him even more. There wasn't the slightest hesitation in the way he helped strangers. His kindness seemed effortless, as though it was simply a part of who he was.

A faint smile appeared on her face.

But almost immediately, it disappeared.

Of all the moments to stop the story, Siddu had chosen the one where the biggest truth was finally about to be revealed.

Now, she had no choice but to patiently wait until the elderly couple reached their destination.

Several hours later, the car finally entered the beautiful hill station of Mussoorie. Surrounded by towering mountains and covered in a pleasant chill, the town welcomed them with its breathtaking scenery.

The elderly couple got down from the car, thanking Siddu repeatedly for his kindness before bidding them goodbye.

As the car began moving again, Siddu turned toward Sneha.

"So," he asked with a smile, "where would you like to go?"

Sneha looked through the window at the snow-covered mountains standing proudly in the distance. Her eyes sparkled with excitement.

"Can we go to one of the hilly regions?" she asked eagerly.

Siddu smiled.

"Sure. Your wish."

A little while later, the two of them found themselves climbing a snow-covered hill. The weather was calm, the cold breeze gently brushing against their faces. Above them stretched an endless blue sky, while soft white clouds floated so low that they seemed close enough to touch.

Neither of them spoke. They simply stood near the top of the hill, letting the silence say what words could not. The cold breeze drifted gently around them while the clouds floated so close that they almost seemed within reach.

Sneha closed her eyes for a moment, taking in the peaceful beauty around her.

As she stepped forward, her foot suddenly slipped on the snow.

Before she could fall, a strong pair of hands caught hold of her.

It was Siddu.

His grip was firm yet gentle, instantly pulling her back to safety.

For a brief moment, time seemed to stand still.

Their eyes met.

Neither of them looked away.

Without realizing it, Sneha slowly drifted closer, still held securely in Siddu's arms.

Siddu's mind suddenly went blank.

In the very next instant, an unexpected memory flashed before his eyes.

The face before him was no longer Sneha's.

It was Shreya.

She stood exactly where Sneha was, looking deep into his eyes with the same silence, the same closeness.

Slowly...

She leaned toward him.

The distance between them grew smaller with every passing second.

Then, just as suddenly as it had appeared, the vision vanished.

Siddu blinked and returned to reality.

His heartbeat skipped a beat as reality came crashing back. Sneha was standing dangerously close, their faces only inches apart, her warm breath brushing against his skin.

Startled, he immediately loosened his grip and gently moved her away from him.

Taking a deep breath, he looked away for a moment, trying to calm the storm of emotions that had suddenly awakened within him.
